messages:
Alex: Heads up — after rolling the control plane to k8s 1.29 in eu-west-1, cluster-autoscaler stopped scaling GPU nodepools for prod clusters. Anyone else seeing this?
Priya: Seeing alerts for training-queue-prod, lots of Pending pods: "0/10 nodes available".
Alex: Autoscaler logs show: "No node groups with GPU capacity found" despite nodepools existing. Quick `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` shows labels changed.
Mateo: paste of `kubectl get nodes` (truncated):
```
NAME                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   LABELS
gpu-node-1          Ready    <none>   2h    node.redwood.io/accelerator=true,topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-west-1a
gpu-node-2          Ready    <none>   2h    node.redwood.io/accelerator=true,topology.kubernetes.io/zone=eu-west-1b
```
Previously those nodes had `node.k8s.redwood.io/gpu=true` which CA looks for.
Jing: I dug into the nodepool-operator conversion logic — the CRD conversion in 1.29 moved the old label key to a new canonical key: `node.redwood.io/accelerator` (we shipped that change upstream). The autoscaler deployment still filters nodegroups by the legacy label. CA is ignoring those pools.
Samir: Confirmed on prod-eu-2 bootstrap logs: our init script was updated to write only `node.redwood.io/accelerator=true`. So new nodes never get the legacy label.
Mateo: Autoscaler log snippet:
```
I0312 10:12:04.123456       1 predicate_checker.go:210] No node groups with GPU capacity found, skipping
```
Priya: Immediate mitigation options? Rollback control plane? Patch CA args? Add compatibility labels on new nodes?
Mateo: Rolling back control plane is risky and slow, plus GPUs are scarce in eu-west right now. I have a small hotfix branch to make CA accept either label (old OR new). That should be a ~30min patch and rollout.
Alex: Good. Also we should write a short mutating job to copy the new label to the legacy key on existing nodes to unblock things quickly.
Jing: I can push a node-bootstrap compatibility job that runs `kubectl label node $NODE node.k8s.redwood.io/gpu=true --overwrite` for nodes with the new key. Also add a DaemonSet that ensures both labels for 48h.
Samir: I'll update the cluster-autoscaler deployment manifest to include the label mappings and add a unit test for the label selector. We'll also file an upstream issue for nodepool-operator so the change is documented. Ticket INFRA-4321 created.
autoscale-bot: deploy started for cluster prod-eu-3 — job/patch-ca-accept-legacy-labels, initiated by Mateo, status: in_progress
Mateo: Patch applied to prod-eu-3 CA deployment. Watching logs/metrics now.
Priya: Confirming: autoscaler picked up GPU nodegroups and initiated scale-up for training-queue-prod. Pods are scheduling. :thumbsup:
Samir: Plan after hotfix: 1) backport CA change to our stable images (1.26/1.27) 2) roll out bootstrap label-copy DS to all clusters 3) update nodepool operator docs and propose a graceful migration path. I'll own rollout, ETA EOD.
Alex: Agreed. Please capture exact commands and logs for a quick postmortem. Jing + Samir to draft. Also add cost note — we saw a few transient extra GPU requests while autoscaler retried; keep an eye on billing.
Mateo: Short checklist I used:
```
# debug
kubectl get nodes --selector='node.redwood.io/accelerator=true' --show-labels
kubectl logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system | grep GPU
# hotfix (deployed via kustomize)
kubectl apply -k overlays/prod/cluster-autoscaler
# bootstrap DS (temporary)
kubectl apply -f manifests/compat-labeler-daemonset.yaml
```
Priya: Thanks — marking incident resolved for now. We'll reopen if scaling fails in the next 2 hours.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft by EOD, include remediation timeline and a follow-up to remove legacy-label copies after 2 weeks.
